chapter_title: Concerning the Fasting of the Saints
spiritual_reading:
#
 Spiritual
 Translation


**
¶4:**

The
 living
 good that
 flows
 into the
 interior
 mind
 through
 the contin
ual reception
 of spiritual
 nourishment —
 that
 is
,
 the appropri
ation of truth
 and good state
 by
 state
, in
 each successive
 illumination — this
 good
 is progress
ively sanctified, freed
 from ev
ils, purified in
 its
 intentions, and reformed
 through tru
ths,
 so
 that the
 falsity which
 had
 been com
mingled with it
,
 and which had ad
ulterated its
 quality
 from
 within
, is at
 last entirely separated
 from it.

**¶5
:**
This
 is
 the hidden
 nature
 of those
 regener
ated through divine
 wisdom:
 in
 their
 interiors there
 is neither
 corruption nor falsification
.
 They
 receive
 what
 is spiritu
ally n
ourishing without
 dimin
ishing or
 inj
uring it. Their
 internal
 states
 are wholly
 consec
rated;
 nothing
 of
 fals
ity or self
-derived
 evil cont
aminates their reception
 of good
. They d
well in peace —
 which
 is the in
most heav
enly state, present
 when love
 and truth
 are fully
 conjoined and
 no
 conflict remains
 between
 them.

**¶6:**

They
 hold
 themselves
 within
 the state
 of spiritual
 trial
 —
 where
 love
 and wisdom
 meet
 and
 are tested
 —
 and they rest
rain their power
 from acting through the comp
uls
ions
 of the
 self
hood. They do not,
 by
 any exercise
 of their own agency
, ext
inguish the living good within truth —
 that
 is, they do not destroy the divine
 life present
 in whatever
 they
 receive
,
 but
 preserve
 it whole
.

reconstructions.reconstructed_text: This soul that comes into him in the administration of his food, day by day; it shall be made holy, cleansed, purified, and washed from the adulteration of the darkness that is mixed in with it.

the mystery of [the children] of light in whom there is neither corruption nor [adulteration. They do not diminish] the food, nor wound it. Rather, they are holy, [there is nothing] in them that defiles, as they live in peace.
